# Dialogs

Dialogs are implemented using
[dbc.Modal](https://dash-bootstrap-components.opensource.faculty.ai/docs/components/modal/).

## Upload dataset dialog

This dialog lets the user upload a dataset from a spreadsheet file.

Components:

- modal:
    - [file uploader](#file-uploader)
    - ok button
    - cancel button

Behavior:

- This dialog is opened/closed through the [upload-dialog-flag](#dialog-flags).
- A file can be uploaded by either clicking the file-uploader or dragging a
  file onto it. Only one file can be uploaded at a time, and the allowed
  formats are CSV and XLSX. When the upload completes, the ok-button is
  enabled.
- The ok-button confirms the upload and proceeds to
  [dataset configuration](#dataset-configuration).
- The cancel-button should discard the uploaded file and close the dialog.
- Clicking outside the dialog closes the dialog.

Callbacks:

- on upload-dialog-flag changed:
    - set modal.is_open
- on data uploaded:
    - store dataset
    - enable ok button
- on ok button clicked:
    - reset upload-dialog-flag
    - set conf-dialog-flag
- on cancel button clicked:
    - delete last dataset
    - reset upload-dialog-flag

# UI Components

This section will go through all the UI components used by the different
screens in the tool. Each sub-section contains the details for a UI component
which includes the following:

- A brief description.
- Its behavior which mainly goes over how the user is allowed to interact with
  it.
- Its API which describes how another component can use it.

## Top bar menu

This is the main-menu bar at the top of every page.

Menu items:

- Upload dataset
- Datasets: *list of datasets*
- View validation profiles
- Tutorials

Behavior:

1.  The bar should be fixed to the top of the screen. Even if the user
    scrolls, the position of the bar should not change.
2.  When the user clicks on the **Upload Dataset** button, the
    [Upload dataset dialog](#upload-dataset-dialog) should be opened.
3.  When the user clicks on the **Datasets** button, a dropdown should
    be opened that lists all the datasets that the user has uploaded.
    The dropdown should be closed when the user clicks on any part of
    the app again.
    1.  Each dataset should be presented to the user using its file
        name.
    2.  When the user clicks on a dataset, it should be selected, and
        the user taken to the [View Dataset page](#view-dataset-page). The dropdown
        should be closed.
    3.  When the user has not uploaded any datasets, the dropdown should
        only have one item that says **No Datasets Uploaded**.
4.  When the user clicks on the **View Validation Profiles** button, the
    [View validation profiles dialog](#view-validation-profiles-dialog) should
    be opened.
5.  The **Tutorials** button can be disabled for now.

Callbacks:

- on upload button clicked:
    - set upload-dialog-flag

## File uploader

This is simply
[dcc.Upload](https://dash.plotly.com/dash-core-components/upload), since we can
get away with uploading to
[dcc.Store](https://dash.plotly.com/dash-core-components/store) only.

# Stores

This section includes the different stores where the app will persist data.
Each sub-section goes over the details of each store and the data stored within
it.

## Memory store

All the data in this store type is stored in browser memory. The data is
transient, meaning that the data is lost when the user reloads/closes the tool.

### Dialog flags

All flags are currently used as signals for showing and hiding dialogs.
There is one flag per dialog, and they are all of type bool.

The reason for having signals/flags is to uncouple components from each other,
so that they don't directly reference each other. This prevents complicated
dependencies and cycles.

The flags are:

- conf-dialog-flag, for the
  [configure dataset dialog](#configure-dataset-dialog)
- upload-dialog-flag, for the
  [upload dataset dialog](#upload-dataset-dialog)

### Datasets

Type: array of [Dataset](#dataset)

This contains all the datasets that the user has uploaded to the tool.

The fact that users cannot edit a dataset in the tool forces them to update it
in their local file system after validation. After making the required changes
to the dataset, they will need to re-upload it to the tool if they wish to
validate it again. This upload, validate, fix, re-upload cycle means that there
is no need to permanently store a dataset in the OPFS store, since it will
always be out of sync with the version on the user’s local file system.

# Types

This section goes over the structure of the different data that the tool will
store.

Common aliases:
```python
OdmTableName = str
TableData = List[dict]  # or pandas.DataFrame
SheetName = str
```

## OdmVersion

Type: enum

Fields:

- v1_0_0
- v1_1_0
- v2_0_0

Underscores are used in place of dots, due to Python naming requirements.

## Dataset

Type: class

Fields:

- `filename: str`

  Used as the datasets unique id. It is shown in the datasets-dropdown in the
  [Top bar menu](#top-bar-menu), and in any screen that is interacting with it.

- `odm_version:` [OdmVersion](#odmversion)

  Detected from the dataset or specified by the user. Required for knowing
  which ODM version to validate against.

- `table_names: Dict[SheetName, OdmTableName]`

  Maps table/sheet names to valid ODM table names. This is the same for CSV and
  Excel files. CSV files have one sheet with the same name as the file.

- `tables: Dict[OdmTableName, TableData]`

  Holds the actual data for each table/sheet.
